claim_one_line: Round two of an outside review under the instruction to verify everything and accept nothing: all three remaining defects confirmed by independent computation, and the referee's one favourable correction is WRONG in our disfavour. (1) The referee reported the verification package passing end to end; on this tree it is 1 failed, 728 passed, and the failing lock is NOT flaky and NOT a timeout -- its script hands a SET to sympy's solver as the list of unknowns, so the answer's normalisation moves with PYTHONHASHSEED. Measured by pulling the pre-fix script back out of git and running both versions under eight seeds: pre-fix passes on seeds 4 and 7 only and fails reproducibly on 0,1,2,3,5,6; post-fix passes on all eight. A reproducible failing set is what separates this from flakiness, and this bench had itself misdiagnosed it as load and RAISED THE TIMEOUT the day before -- a wrong fix that would have left it failing three runs in four forever. Minted as E83 and swept over 3 872 tracked files: 34 order-sensitive sites, five shipped locks among them, all five run under five seeds and stable. (2) Exactly 1 of 57 chain-table rows disagreed with the generator that emits it -- the Weinberg miss as 0.9 per cent where the generator says 0.8 -- because the generated block was corrected but never re-spliced, and the gate that exists to catch this read rows[:6] + rows[-3:], nine of 57, with the stale row in the 48 it skipped. A drift gate that samples can only see drift at the ends; it now reads every row. (3) MANIFEST.json named a commit that resolves on this bench and nowhere else -- built before a commit that was then amended -- and the previous day's check that its 147 locks were present PASSED ONLY BECAUSE IT RAN AGAINST THAT DANGLING OBJECT: a check made against something only the author can see is not a check. The manifest now records whether HEAD is published and a lock asserts it. (4) The runner's 'Overall: PASS' was hollow on a partial run; the verdict now names its coverage and refuses the unqualified word unless all three steps ran. (5) Found here rather than reported: the retractions index the paper cites BY COUNT had drifted -- neither of the last two corrections had a row, because retraction-debt fires only on arcs whose own verdict says RETRACTED and both had landed as addenda on the arcs that erred, which is the form this record recommends; so the index lags precisely for corrections done the right way. Rows written, count now 29, paper and generator updated, and a lock pins the paper's spelled-out number to the index's row count with a bite control. (6) Owner-raised: an outside report measured main at 101 commits and reasoned structurally from it. Main has 3457 commits, identical on both mirrors, no shallow marker, no grafts; the audit lane's 2965 is its total INCLUDING main's shared history, 110 unique since a fork from the same root commit dated 2026-09-05. 101 commits back reaches 2026-09-14, four days. The truncation was the reader's, but nothing shipped let them notice, and two package checks answer wrongly and silently on a shallow clone; the manifest now records the history length and shallowness, the runner warns into the report when its clone is shorter, and the README gives the full-clone command. Third instance of one shape: a check satisfiable by an incomplete view of the evidence is not a check. (7)+(8) Found by running the full suite to completion, which the landing ritual does not: fourteen arc verdicts violate the schema (seven with the non-enum word VERIFIED, seven missing the creates_law/identifications declarations), unseen because gates.py answers 33/33 in seconds while this test runs only in a 90-minute suite that had not completed since the consolidation; and B1411's committed receipt ends in a Traceback and an AssertionError while its claim says its locks re-ran green, so E83's failure was not merely undiagnosed but PUBLISHED AS EVIDENCE for three days. Both repaired, the failing receipt preserved; a sweep of 1458 tracked receipts finds 47 with a failure marker of which 15 are silent, registered as L223. (9) The suite's remaining failures were four locks pinning states the record had legitimately moved past, all red before this session: one reads a seat branch deleted at the retirement (tag then delete -- a retirement had broken a receipt), one asserts a relay backlog is still open and went red when the backlog was paid, and two pin corpus statistics including a list of seven ideas asserted to remain absent of which four have entered. All rewritten to their durable facts with the drift named in the test. Eighteen red locks in total that the landing ritual could not see; the suite went 22 failures to 1, and that one is the manifest, rebuilt after the commit.
